components.gap: Reconstruct Milton 2011 'Induction before Hume' (HHL vol.10 ch.1, pp.1-41, held PDF) in the owned body/annex: its treatment of the terminology of induction/epagoge/inductio and semeiosis; sec.1 The Ancient World (Gideon example, Socrates and Plato, Aristotle, Hellenistic and later Greek accounts, Roman philosophy); sec.2 The Middle Ages (Arabic accounts, the Latin West); sec.3 The Renaissance (revival of rhetoric, Zabarella); sec.4 seventeenth/early eighteenth century (Bacon incl. eliminative induction and the Limited Variety presupposition, Descartes Regulae Rule VII enumeration, Gassendi, Arnauld and Nicole, Hobbes and Wallis, Leibniz); sec.5 Conclusion -- with every actual definition, argument case, example and separating boundary, preserving presentation-specific qualifications. No handbook file treats this chapter; the only route file for 164.2 explicitly treats Hume's 1777 Enquiry instead (line 1 comment, lines 23-31).

Preserve Milton's full historical argument, source chronology (ancient through Leibniz) and the materially different interpretations he records (e.g. Asmis vs Barnes on applying 'induction' to Hellenistic sign-inference; Hume-as-inductive-sceptic readings), reconstructing every actual definition, inference form and example of the complete chapter without modernizing historical systems or promoting cited boundaries to proofs. Nothing on the handbook route does this.

Give Milton's worked cases (e.g. Gideon's fleece, Aristotle's examples, Bacon's tables/eliminative procedure, Descartes's sufficient and ordered enumeration), limitations and comparisons between authors, stating hypotheses of any modern reconstruction and keeping philosophical, mathematical and empirical claim types distinct. Nothing on the handbook route does this.
